answer: Tax correlation, not identity. Each epoch the node embeds every answer and grade, then any pair of keys whose outputs sit above a similarity ridge shares one payout, split between them. A raven-like operator flocking N keys from one model and prompt sees them merge into one umber blur and earns once; to collect N rewards it must pay for N genuinely distinct models, prompts and timing habits, a cost that grows per key while honest independent agents lose nothing.
